model_priors.model_reasoning: TNFRSF17 (BCMA, B-cell maturation antigen) is a well-characterized TNF receptor superfamily member expressed on plasma cells and B cells. It is the receptor for APRIL and BAFF. BCMA is well-known in the literature for constitutive, rapid internalization — it has one of the highest basal endocytic rates among TNFRSF members, which is why it is a challenging ADC target and why surface levels are low despite high mRNA expression. The canonical isoform has a single-pass type I topology with a substantial cytoplasmic tail (~108 aa). Inspection of the cytoplasmic tail reveals a YKSL sequence (Y at position ~168, context YCKSL) that resembles a YXX[hydrophobic] motif, as well as the overall length of the cytoplasmic domain that is permissive for adaptor interactions. Beyond motifs, the known biology of BCMA strongly supports high constitutive internalization: surface BCMA is shed/internalized rapidly, and soluble BCMA in serum is a biomarker of plasma cell burden partly reflecting this turnover. The protein's known behavior dominates the assessment.

per_isoform.topology_summary: Single-pass type I transmembrane protein; N-terminus extracellular (~53 aa), single TM helix, C-terminus cytoplasmic (~108 aa).
per_isoform.endocytic_motifs_noted: Cytoplasmic tail (~aa 77–184): contains a YCKSL sequence (Y168 context) resembling a YXX[hydrophobic] internalization motif; the long cytoplasmic tail (108 aa) is generally permissive for adaptor/ubiquitin-mediated uptake. No canonical NPXY or dileucine [DE]XXXL[LI] motifs clearly identified, but motif absence is not limiting given known biology.
per_isoform.rationale: BCMA (TNFRSF17) is one of the most rapidly internalizing members of the TNFRSF. Its constitutive endocytosis is well-established: surface expression is low relative to transcript levels, soluble BCMA is shed into serum as a consequence of rapid turnover, and the protein internalizes constitutively as well as upon APRIL/BAFF binding. The 108-aa cytoplasmic tail provides ample opportunity for adaptor interactions. A YXX[hydrophobic]-like motif is present in the cytoplasmic region. Taken together, known biology and sequence features both strongly support a high intrinsic internalization grade.
